finding: Several risk and protective factors for structural and functional damage to anal sphincters were identified postpartum in Sri Lankan primigravida, including mode of delivery, episiotomy, and neonatal factors.
mod_finding: Episiotomy was protective against anal sphincter damage, while delivering after 40 weeks' gestation and delivering a baby with a longer length increased the risk of sphincter pressure reduction; EAS defects were more common in mothers who had labor augmented by oxytocin and in those who delivered a baby with a larger head circumference, while labor induction and delivering a longer baby were protective for EAS defects.
